issues.issue: Is the judicial review of the December 2024 TRV refusal moot after IRCC reopened and redetermined the application?
issues.applicant_position: Not moot: the Court should decide the judicial review and send the matter back; reopening does not end the dispute.
issues.respondent_position: Minister says the reopening and June 2026 refusal were valid; matter not moot only because costs are undecided.
issues.result_quote: I therefore conclude that IRCC’s decision to reopen and redetermine Mr. Gill’s TRV application, despite having been made in error, rendered this application moot.

issues.issue: Should the Court exercise its residual discretion to decide the moot application?
issues.applicant_position: Adversarial context exists and judicial economy favours deciding the fully argued matter.
issues.result_quote: For the following reasons, I conclude that the Court should not exercise its residual discretion to hear the matter.

issues.issue: Is there a basis for a costs award on this application?
issues.applicant_position: Requests costs in the leave application and memorandum.
issues.respondent_position: Treated costs as an undecided issue keeping the matter live (para 9).
issues.result_quote: there is no basis for the Court to grant such an award

issues.issue: Should the applicant be granted an extension of time to seek leave on the June 2026 refusal?
issues.applicant_position: Seeks extension; says the June 2026 refusal was not filed on time because of unclear status.
issues.respondent_position: Consents to the extension; no prejudice to the Minister.
issues.result_quote: I conclude there are special reasons to grant Mr. Gill an extension of time to apply for leave and for judicial review of the June 2026 refusal
